issues.description: Element: field 'lectureName' of class Lecture. Problem statement (UML) declares lectureName as type String (problem_statement.md UML fields). The solution repository declares a field of type LectureName (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) and introduces a separate LectureName class (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/LectureName.java). This mismatch also appears in the solution constructor parameter (constructor takes LectureName) and in getter/setter implementations where signatures and returned/assigned values are inconsistent, producing compile-time type contradictions. This will confuse students about the expected type for lectureName and can cause compilation errors if the solution is used as reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of lectureName consistent with the problem statement UML (String) across the solution: change the field to 'private String lectureName;', update the constructor parameter to accept String (and keep the order specified in the UML), and update getter/setter implementations to use String. Remove the auxiliary LectureName class (or adapt all references consistently if you prefer a value object) so that field type, constructor signature and accessor signatures align with the exercise specification. Alternatively, if the author intends to use a LectureName value object, update the problem statement/UML to specify LectureName and make all getter/setter signatures return/accept LectureName consistently.
